solution.solution: An overnight plugin, which rn uses, that starts a run of rn at night as a batch in its own process, `claude -p`, under claude-ac (https://github.com/blackstardigitalstudio/claude-auto-continue, MIT), which watches the output for the usage-limit message, waits until the stated reset, and resumes the same session with `--continue`, so the stop and the resume stay in the conversation's history for the morning; where the run comes to a point that is the user's to decide, it stops there and leaves the point as a question for the morning.
solution.why: The user rejected Claude Code's own `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` as unreliable, and it is never offered in `-p` runs, so it can't serve a separate-process batch at all; claude-ac already does the watching, waiting, and resuming in `-p` runs on macOS and Linux under the MIT license, so rn makes only the thin start that runs rn under it, rather than a watcher of its own or Codeman, which does more than this need.

assumption.assumption: A run of rn started at night by the overnight plugin goes on in its own process with no one there: no permission prompt stops it, claude-ac recognizes the current Claude Code's usage-limit message and resumes the same session after the reset, and by morning the run has reached its end or a question for the user.
assumption.test: On the user's machine, start a real run of rn with the overnight plugin at night and leave it until it meets the usage limit; in the morning, check that it reached its end or a question, and that the session's history shows when it stopped and when it resumed.

opportunities.opportunity: In the morning, I want to see what stopped at the limit and what resumed.
opportunities.by: The user's answer to Q2 of the hearing on 2026-11-27

decisions.decision: The run is for a user who instructs an AI and leaves the AI to arrange the work, as the user answered 「ユーザーがAIに指示してAIが段取る」.
Once the limit lifts, the stopped work goes on from where it stopped, and a record remains of what stopped and what resumed, as the user answered 「１と２」.
The aim is that work moves on while the user sleeps and in the morning they only check the results, as the user answered 「１」.
Making the stopped work go on from where it stopped is also to show in the morning what stopped and what resumed, as the user asked 「１やったら２やることにならないの？」 and called the opposite 「そんなおかしな話ある？」.

rn stays a tool the user works with in conversation, and the night's work is a batch in a separate process that rn starts, as the user said 「rnは対話で作業する前提だよね」, 「rnからオーバーナイトを使うようなイメージ」, and 「別プロセスで夜に作業するバッチのようなイメージ」.
The resume relies on an outside watcher, not on Claude Code's `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, as the user answered 「autoContinueAtUsageLimitはあてにならない」 and 「２かな」.

A night's batch stops at each point that is the user's to decide and leaves it as a question for the morning, since rn asks the user what is theirs and fills no gap by guessing, and no one answers at night.

Before the overnight plugin runs claude-ac, the maker reads every file of claude-ac that runs and shows the user what it reads, writes, runs, and sends out, as the user's rules ask of another author's tool.
The talk is in Japanese, the language of the user's words, and the deliverables are in English, the language of the repository's documents, so each reader reads their own.

steps.settles: rnから夜に別プロセスのバッチを始め、使用量の上限で止まっても、上限が解けたら止まったところから続く。
